investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 05:41 and 05:49 UTC on 2026-07-09 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes had zero schedulable capacity for kata.peerpods.io/vm pods, with 2 nodes reporting insufficient VM quota and 4 nodes failing node affinity/selector matching. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were never written, causing a complete contract gap.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm (production-api environment) had exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, while the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector requirements. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable for ~144–146 seconds before the eval timed out. No VM was ever allocated, so no agent identity or state was produced, and the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was entirely unmet. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity failure localized to the kata peer-pods node pool, not an application code defect.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote-agent VMs from prior runs or other workloads consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new pods. Preemption found no victims, indicating no lower-priority pods were present to evict.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift on 4 of 6 nodes: those nodes may have lost the label or taint required by the remote-agent pod spec, reducing the schedulable pool from 6 to 2 nodes and amplifying the quota exhaustion impact.

Tertiary — a prior eval run or cleanup failure left orphaned remote-agent VMs running on the 2 kata-capable nodes, consuming the VM quota without being released. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1883) is responsible for teardown; a failed cleanup could leave quota held.

Lower confidence — transient node pool scaling lag: the kata peer-pod node pool may not have auto-scaled in time to absorb the eval's pod requests, though the preemption message ('No preemption victims found') suggests quota exhaustion rather than a scaling delay alone.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-09T05:44–05:49Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the production cluster's 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes have no remaining VM slots, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes that support the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource class reported Insufficient capacity (no free VM slots), and the other 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both capacity-bearing nodes. This infrastructure-level scheduling blockage prevented agent creation entirely, which is the upstream cause of all missing required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) and the resulting eval contract failure. This is an eval-detected infrastructure signal, not a confirmed user-facing outage, as no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion: the 2 nodes that carry the VM resource class have no remaining capacity and no preemptible pods, so no new remote agent pod can be admitted. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on remaining 4 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 VM-capable nodes satisfy; those 4 nodes are structurally ineligible regardless of capacity.

Tertiary — concurrent or leaked agent pods consuming all VM slots: if prior eval runs or user workloads left agent pods running without cleanup, the VM resource pool would be depleted before this run began. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1903) is intended to prevent this, but a prior crash or timeout could have bypassed cleanup.

Lower confidence — node affinity configuration drift: a change to the pod's node selector or to node labels could have reduced the eligible node set, but no suspect change touching pod specs is present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges (which is empty).

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 05:41 and 05:49 UTC on 2026-07-09 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes had zero schedulable capacity for kata.peerpods.io/vm pods, with 2 nodes reporting insufficient VM quota and 4 nodes failing node affinity/selector matching. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were never written, causing a complete contract gap.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm (production-api environment) had exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, while the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector requirements. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable for ~144–146 seconds before the eval timed out. No VM was ever allocated, so no agent identity or state was produced, and the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was entirely unmet. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity failure localized to the kata peer-pods node pool, not an application code defect.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote-agent VMs from prior runs or other workloads consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new pods. Preemption found no victims, indicating no lower-priority pods were present to evict.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift on 4 of 6 nodes: those nodes may have lost the label or taint required by the remote-agent pod spec, reducing the schedulable pool from 6 to 2 nodes and amplifying the quota exhaustion impact.

Tertiary — a prior eval run or cleanup failure left orphaned remote-agent VMs running on the 2 kata-capable nodes, consuming the VM quota without being released. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1883) is responsible for teardown; a failed cleanup could leave quota held.

Lower confidence — transient node pool scaling lag: the kata peer-pod node pool may not have auto-scaled in time to absorb the eval's pod requests, though the preemption message ('No preemption victims found') suggests quota exhaustion rather than a scaling delay alone.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-09T05:44–05:49Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the production cluster's 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes have no remaining VM slots, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes that support the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource class reported Insufficient capacity (no free VM slots), and the other 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both capacity-bearing nodes. This infrastructure-level scheduling blockage prevented agent creation entirely, which is the upstream cause of all missing required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) and the resulting eval contract failure. This is an eval-detected infrastructure signal, not a confirmed user-facing outage, as no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Exhaustion: kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Insufficient Across All 3 Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-09T05:44–05:49Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both were already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, no agent was created, and the runtime eval produced zero evidence — all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent eval environment has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm peer-pod VM capacity. Of the 6 available nodes, only 2 are eligible to run kata peer-pod workloads, and both reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" at scheduling time. The remaining 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption could not help because no lower-priority victims were found on the 2 eligible nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~144–146 seconds before the eval timed out, preventing agent creation entirely and causing all downstream evidence collection (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) to fail. This is an eval-infrastructure / cluster-capacity failure localized to the remote-agents feature in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

Lower probability — the 2 kata-eligible nodes were temporarily cordoned, drained, or undergoing maintenance at the time of the eval run, reducing available capacity to zero without a resource exhaustion event.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeds and produces all 5 required evidence fields, it would indicate the capacity issue was transient (e.g., a competing workload finished) rather than a sustained exhaustion.

If kubectl or cluster tooling shows that the 2 kata-eligible nodes have unused kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity at the time of the failure, the scheduling error message would need an alternative explanation (e.g., a quota or admission webhook rejection misreported as resource exhaustion).

If the 4 non-eligible nodes are shown to have been recently relabeled or had their affinity requirements changed so they now match the pod selector, the root cause would shift to a node configuration drift rather than capacity exhaustion.

If no other pods were consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots at the time of the failure, the cause would shift to the 2 eligible nodes being cordoned, drained, or in a NotReady state rather than resource exhaustion.

If the local-agent-runtime or local-agent-create checks (which do not use kata.peerpods.io/vm) also failed at the same time, it would suggest a broader API or authentication failure rather than a kata peer-pod capacity issue.
